To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

museums are (being) continuously changing and will change in the future, and that they will change in a way that is driven by the intertwining helices of museum of the (artistic) future and the future of museums (in the knowledge society).
museums will continue to play a key role in the future.
museums are continuously changing, and they must change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the future of museums in the knowledge society and knowledge democracy, in the knowledge economy, in the digital age.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the museum of the present is a museum of the future.
the museum of the Future and future of museums is an ongoing process of change and evolution, and that this is not an issue of the future, but of the present.
the museum of the (near) future is a museum of art, science, and society, of knowledge, of innovation and creativity, of virtuality, of networks, of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
museums of the future must be future museums.
the museum of the present and the future will be the museum of the past, present, and future.
museums are continuously of importance, but they have to be open for changes and for new developments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the museum of the (near) future and the future of museums are not only of importance for museums, but for the society at large.
the museum of the Future will have to be an open, inclusive, and participatory museum that is able to adapt to the changing needs of society and the environment.
museums will be and should be important for art and society in the future.
